articles.title: Bigg Boss Malayalam 8: Neha fears post-show criticism, parents assure her, ‘We are always with you’
articles.summary: Family Week in Bigg Boss Malayalam 8 brought a heartwarming reunion for Neha as her parents entered the house.
articles.body: Family Week in Bigg Boss Malayalam 8 brought a heartwarming reunion for Neha as her parents entered the house. Following their unexpected appearance during a weekend episode and the emotional moments that followed, Neha was visibly overwhelmed when she saw her mother and father. Unable to hold back her tears, she broke down as she hugged them, making their reunion one of the most emotional moments of the week.During their interaction, Neha’s mother reminded her that many people were supporting her outside the house. She said, “There are so many people supporting you. They all loved the way you played during the first two weeks.” She also encouraged Neha to play independently and reminded her that only a few weeks remained in the competition.At one point, her mother told her, “You have to come home, okay?” The remark appeared to touch an emotional chord with Neha, who had earlier broken down when the family videos were played inside the house. As her parents’ video was not played during that segment, Neha became emotional and wondered where she would go if she could not return home.Responding to her mother’s words, Neha admitted, “I was really scared. That’s why I said I wouldn’t come home. But then I thought, where else would I go? Where can I go other than my own home?” She also expressed concern about what the neighbours and relatives might say about her after the show.Offering reassurance, Neha’s mother said, “There are so many people coming home just to see you and talk to you. The neighbours really like you. Everyone is very supportive and happy for you. So don’t think about all that.”Neha then told her parents, “As long as I have you both with me, I don’t care even if someone criticises me. Even if the entire world criticises me, it doesn’t matter to me.”Responding to her daughter’s concerns, Neha’s father said, “It is not really those people who are criticising you. It is a few people on social media. Why are they criticising you? It is only to generate revenue. But even if they criticise you, what is the problem when we are with you?” He once again assured her that the family would always stand by her.For the unversed, Neha’s emotional journey in the Bigg Boss house took a turn following her parents’ unexpected appearance during a weekend episode. During the family video segment, she was particularly upset when her parents’ video was not played, and she broke down while wondering whether she would be able to return home.Get the latest TV News, TV Shows and more. articles.title: 'Father of iPod' Tony Fadell says that Sam Altman asked 'iPhone designer' Jony Ive to build a physical device for OpenAI as he knows that Apple will never …
articles.summary: Sam Altman asked Jony Ive to build an AI device.
articles.body: ​Sam Altman asked Jony Ive to build an AI device. Tony Fadell, the former Apple executive also known as the “father of the iPod,” says the reason comes down to what Apple lets OpenAI learn from the iPhone. Speaking to*Fortune at Web Summit in Lisbon, Fadell said Apple’s privacy restrictions limit the information ChatGPT can gather about a user’s surroundings.​“They have to build products because they cannot get contextual information out of the phone,” Fadell said. He argued that building its own device would let OpenAI use microphones, cameras, GPS and other sensors to give ChatGPT more context. In his view, knowing more about what’s happening around a user could help the assistant answer faster and more accurately.​Why Sam Altman says AI needs a new kind of device​OpenAI pointed Fortune to a video in which Altman gave his own explanation. “The reason we want to do new kinds of consumer hardware is that I think this is a technology that wants a new form factor,” he said. Altman argued that phones and laptops are designed around interfaces people can see and navigate. An AI agent using those same interfaces may have to interpret what’s on the screen to reach information it could otherwise access directly.​Ive, Apple's former design Guru, started working with Altman and OpenAI through his design company LoveFrom. In July 2025, OpenAI announced that io, Ive’s hardware startup, was acquired by the company. Ive and LoveFrom stayed independent and took on design work across OpenAI.​What OpenAI’s device could look like​Fadell said one possibility is a screenless companion device with its own sensors. It could connect over Wi-Fi or Bluetooth and pass information to an AI agent running in the cloud or on a phone. He also pointed to the potential for edge computing, where simpler AI tasks run on a nearby device instead of making a round trip to a remote server.​Fadell floated several forms, including a pendant, a pen and a speaker. Each could collect a different kind of information about what a user is doing or what’s happening nearby. As Fadell put it, “they’re just trying to get context.” ​Fearless legend or grounded realist? articles.title: Tarun Khanna to play Lord Shiva in the play ‘Bholenath Aur Unke Bhakt’
articles.summary: Producer Shameem Faridi is set to collaborate with actor Tarun Khanna for the play ‘Bholenath Aur Unke Bhakt’, in which Khanna will essay the title role.
articles.body: Producer Shameem Faridi is set to collaborate with actor Tarun Khanna for the play ‘Bholenath Aur Unke Bhakt’, in which Khanna will essay the title role. The two share a long association, dating back to 2007. Recalling his journey in the entertainment industry, Faridi says he moved to Mumbai in 2001 without any film connections. He initially worked in marketing before finding his footing in the industry.With an educational background in finance, Faridi also worked in accounts before joining Archana Puran Singh’s company, where he handled arrangements on sets. He later joined Aruna Irani’s production house as an Assistant Manager.Talking about his upcoming play with Khanna, Faridi reveals that the initial plan was to stage a production on Chanakya. However, he eventually felt that Khanna, known for portraying Lord Shiva, would be ideal for the project.“Initially, we were thinking of coming up with a play on Chanakya, but then I thought of Tarun Khanna, who is known for his portrayal of Lord Shiva. I have known Tarun since 2007, when I was working on ‘Kittu Sab Janti Hain’. He is like an elder brother to me. Our discussions have taken shape, and we are now at the final stage of the announcement. We can't wait to begin production,” he says.Get the latest TV News, TV Shows and more. Download the TOI app.

articles.title: The SE 3 is the Apple Watch most people should buy on Black Friday
articles.summary: The Apple Watch SE 3, which includes most of the health-tracking features found on more expensive models, is on sale for Black Friday starting at $179 ($70 off).
articles.body: During Black Friday, the Apple Watch SE 3 is on sale in the 40mm / GPS configuration at Amazon, Walmart, and Target starting around $179 ($70 off), $20 less than its previous lowest price. The 44mm variant, meanwhile, is on sale at Amazon, Walmart, and Target starting at around $209 (also $70 off), also beating its previous low by $20. [Product: Apple Watch SE 3 | Despite having launched over a year ago, the Apple Watch SE 3 is still the Apple Watch model we recommend for most people. It includes many of the trademark features of higher-end Apple Watch models like the Series 12, including an always-on display, double-tap and wrist flick gestures, fast-charging, and on-device Siri. The compromise is that the SE 3 lacks some of the more advanced health features found on more expensive models, like blood oxygen and EKG sensing. The battery life also isn’t quite as strong, but if you don’t need as many health-tracking sensors, it’s a much better value, especially at this price. Read our Apple Watch SE 3 review.

articles.title: The Oura Ring 5 just got its biggest discount ever for Black Friday
articles.summary: The Oura Ring 5, which is hands down the best smart ring available, is on sale for $100 off for Black Friday, dropping it to an all-time low of $299.
articles.body: If you’ve been curious about smart rings but have been put off by their high price tags, Black Friday is a good time to consider giving one a try. That’s because the Oura Ring 5, which we consider the best smart ring you can buy, has dropped to an all-time low of $299 ($100 off) at Amazon, Best Buy, Walmart, and Oura’s online storefront for Black Friday. [Product: Oura Ring 5 | Compared to the Ring 4, the Oura Ring 5 offers a thinner, lighter, and more durable design that’s more comfortable to wear throughout the day and while sleeping. Like its predecessor, it can track your sleep, activity, heart rate, and other health metrics, giving you insights into your overall well-being without requiring you to constantly check a screen. It also offers roughly the same battery life and sensors as the prior model, though its new charging case supports wireless charging. (Unfortunately, the case is currently sold separately for $99.) Oura has also introduced several new software features, including Health Radar, which looks for potentially significant changes in your health. You can also import medical lab results, track GLP-1 medications, and access AI-assisted medical guidance through Oura’s partnership with Counsel Health. My colleague Victoria Song appreciated how the latter makes it easier to connect with an actual doctor, though she found it better suited for quick medical questions than more serious health concerns. However, none of these software features are exclusive to the Ring 5, and you’ll still need a $5.99 monthly Oura membership to access most of its health insights. Given how similar the two generations are, we wouldn’t recommend upgrading if you already own a Ring 4. But if you’re new to smart rings, the current discount makes Oura’s latest model much more attractive, especially since it’s only $50 more than the Ring 4’s starting price. articles.title: Android’s DIY widgets are a bit of vibe-coding fun
articles.summary: Google’s new Create My Widget tool lets you turn your homescreen into a highly customizable dashboard — but don’t expect too much from it.
articles.body: Aside from dealing with my calendar, there’s one thing I want AI to do: tell me if I’m about to miss the bus. What I need is a widget. It needs to tell me real-time arrivals for the bus stop near my house. Tapping around on my phone screen to open the right app and select my stop will slow me down enough to miss a bus. I need glanceable information, and I hoped that Android’s vibe-coded widget feature could help me out here. It hasn’t, to my disappointment, but I still had a good time cooking up other widgets. Google announced the ability to create custom widgets using AI back at I/O in the spring. It’s called Create My Widget, and it’s part of Android’s suite of “Gemini Intelligence” features. It’s in beta, and only just started rolling out to Pixel phones earlier this month. I was hyped. Not only does this feature raise tantalizing questions like “What is an app?” and “Where does the app live?” — stuff we live for here at The Verge dot com — it has potential to help me make my home screen ridiculous. I fired it up on a Pixel 11 Pro and cooked up my first few widgets, including one that shows a different quote from Jurassic Park every hour — the original film, not any of the sequels, naturally. It took about 20 seconds to make, and it rules. Tapping the widget opens a thread in r/MovieQuotes, so there’s not much software magic going on under the hood, evidently. But did it bring me real joy to read the words “That is one big pile of shit,” on my home screen? It did. I also made a widget that will display the words “Tut tut, looks like rain” whenever it’s raining. This is silly, and it accomplishes nothing except making me happy. I couldn’t think of anything clever it should say when there’s no rain, so it just says “No rain right now” otherwise. But I live in Seattle, so I’ll get a lot of mileage out of this widget. [Image: [Image: [Image: [Image: The create-a-widget interface suggests a few ideas and categories, leaning on more practical uses like habit trackers and recipe inspiration. Fine, I’ll try something normal, I thought. I’m trying to get better about my daily mental health walk, so I had it make a widget for logging a week’s worth of walks. I was hoping for something visual that would trick my little monkey brain into keeping a streak going. Instead, I got something simply labeled “Log Walk” that triggers Gemini to add a walk to my calendar when I tap it. At least Gemini suggested the extra step of creating a checklist where I could mark off the days of the week as I completed my little walk. It took me a minute to get my head around it, but many of the widgets are basically little prompt shortcuts for Gemini. You tap one, it pulls up the Gemini interface on your home screen, thinks for a while, then comes up with whatever you were asking for. The kinds of widgets you can make also seem to fit into some well-defined templates. You can create a widget that displays a countdown to a holiday or certain event on your calendar. You can show a recent score and upcoming game time for your favorite sports team. For anything more open ended, your widget will pull from Google search results (suggest a different three-ingredient cocktail recipe every day, for example) or prompt Gemini to figure it out for you. I was hoping for mini apps I could customize to my liking, but this is more of a one-size-fits-all feature. Fair, I guess. That’s why my bus schedule widget didn’t really work out. I asked for a list of real-time arrivals; it gave me a tile that reads “Bus Arrivals” and uses Gemini to search for arrival times for the stop I specified. Gemini is helpful for some things but useless for this; it gives me a wordy response about how often the bus runs and when I might expect it to arrive based on the schedule. Not what I had in mind. On the bright side, my Jurassic Park quote widget had some words of wisdom for me: “Life, uh, finds a way.” That’ll do for now.

articles.title: Buying a laptop right now is rough, but these Black Friday deals help
articles.summary: Black Friday is here, bringing with it discounts on MacBooks, Windows machines, gaming laptops, and even new NVIDIA RTX Spark models.
articles.body: Laptop prices have been a hot-button topic all year long thanks to RAMageddon. We’ve seen existing models get more expensive and new models arrive at higher prices than last-gen — sometimes with lower specs, too. 2026 in general has been a bad time to buy a computer. But thankfully, Black Friday can offer a tiny bit of respite. If the computer you currently use is working well for you, good. Happy for you. But if you’re in the market for something more powerful, bigger, smaller, thinner, etc. — and you prefer new over used — you can currently save some decent dough on MacBooks, Windows notebooks, and gaming laptops. The big, multi-hundred-dollar savings are typically reserved for higher-end models with bigger specs, like Windows models running Nvidia’s new Arm-based RTX Spark platform — which are getting their first major discounts. More budget-friendly laptops are also receiving decent discounts right now, though, including the MacBook Neo. The current $100 discount on Apple’s budget laptop might seem like small potatoes considering it’s just a return to its original price, but it’s the best you can do for now (if you can’t hold out for a rumored new one in 2027). As always, the deals below are for laptops we’ve reviewed or tested firsthand in some way at The Verge — either that exact model or a similar one we expect to be equally good. There are many laptops out there and myriad deals running now through Cyber Monday, but if any of these fit your needs, you can’t go wrong. articles.title: You can grab a 12-pack of Zepath’s rechargeable AA batteries for just $24
articles.summary: You can buy Zepath’s 3,000mWh rechargeable lithium AA batteries starting at just $15.99 ($4 off) for Black Friday, which is a new low price.
articles.body: If you’re picking up any gifts that require AA batteries, it’s not a bad idea to buy a set you can keep using long after the holidays. Thankfully, you can currently get a 12-pack of Zepath’s rechargeable 3,000mWh AAs on Amazon with a charger for $23.99 ($8 off) for Black Friday, which is a new low. If you don’t need as many, Amazon is also selling an eight-pack under a different name for just $15.99 ($4 off). [Product: Zepath USB-C Li-ion AA Batteries | My colleague Sean Hollister tested Zepath’s higher-capacity 3,600mWh batteries against competing lithium-ion AAs in April, and he picked them as his top choice. In his tests, they even outlasted Panasonic’s pricier Eneloop Pros in both a Game Boy Advance and a high-powered flashlight. Zepath also says the batteries deliver a steady 1.5V until they’re nearly empty and hold their charge well when not in use. The best part about Zepath’s rechargeables, though, is how you charge them. Instead of relying on a multi-headed USB-C cable that plugs into each cell, you simply drop them into the included clamshell charging case, like a pair of AirPods or a similar set of wireless earbuds. The case also charges via USB-C, so you can top off eight batteries at once with a single connection in about two and a half hours.

articles.title: The best Black Friday deals on AirPods, MacBooks, and other Apple gear
articles.summary: We’ve scoured the web for the best Black Friday deals on Apple products and accessories, many of which are likely to be discounted through the holiday weekend.
articles.body: Black Friday is one of the best times of the year to save some cash on a new pair of AirPods or the latest Apple Watch. After all, the holiday savings can help offset the unfortunate price hikes from earlier this year, when Apple raised the cost of some of its most popular gear. Some discounts even extend to recent releases like the Apple Watch Series 12 and touchscreen MacBook Pro, which have dropped to new lows. In addition to a variety of discounts across retailers, Apple is offering up to $300 in gift cards with select purchases between November 27th and November 30th. How much you get back is determined by how much you spend, with up to $100 available for some iPhone and Apple Watch purchases, and up to $300 for the 16-inch MacBook Pro. That said, in some cases you may be able to save more by buying from other retailers. Featured Products AirPods Pro 3 Apple iPad (11th-gen) Apple Watch Series 12 MacBook Neo Beats 360 headphones Apple AirTag (second-gen) Earbud and headphone deals [Product: AirPods Pro 3 | [Product: Beats Powerbeats Pro 2 | * You can buy the AirPods 4 on sale at Walmart for around $89 ($40 off), which is $20 shy of their best price. Apple’s last-gen earbuds lack active noise cancellation, but they still deliver good, relatively bass-rich sound, even if they don’t quite match the newer AirPods 5. They also offer voice call quality on par with the latest AirPods Pro. Read our review. * The second-gen AirPods Max are down to $419 ($130 off) at Amazon and Best Buy, which is $19 shy of their best price to date (Target also has them for about $10 more). Like the original, Apple’s latest over-ear headphones feature a luxurious build consisting of aluminum, steel, and a mesh fabric, but they offer better sound and noise cancellation. The new H2 chip also enables features like adaptive audio and live translation. Read our review. [Product: Beats Studio Pro | [Product: Beats 360 headphones | * If you want over-ears and are comfortable going without active noise cancellation, the Beats Solo 4 are on sale starting at $79.99 ($120 off) at Amazon and Target — a new low price. The headphones are a noticeable improvement over their predecessor, delivering more detailed sound and support for lossless audio. They also last up to 50 hours on a single charge, while their memory foam ear cushions make them comfortable enough for long listening sessions. Read our review. * The Beats Studio Buds Plus are down to around $89.95 ($80 off) at Amazon, Best Buy, and Target, nearly matching their lowest price to date. The wireless earbuds feature a slick, eye-catching transparent option and solid noise cancellation, especially at this price. They’re also exceptionally comfortable, with four ear tip sizes to help you find a secure fit. Sure, you don’t get wireless charging, but they offer IPX4 water resistance and up to nine hours of battery life on a single charge. Read our review. MacBook deals [Product: MacBook Neo | * The recently released 16.3-inch MacBook Pro with a PROLED XDR display, 24GB of RAM, and 1TB of storage is on sale starting at $3,099 ($300 off) — a new low price — at Amazon. The redesigned laptop is Apple’s first with an OLED touchscreen, which allows for rich colors and deep blacks. It’s also noticeably thinner and lighter than the non-touchscreen 16-inch MacBook Pro, and features a new Dynamic Island that replaces the notch and provides quick access to controls and notifications. Read our review. [Product: Apple MacBook Air (M5) | * The 14-inch M6-powered MacBook Pro is on sale starting at $1,749 ($250 off) at Amazon and Best Buy, which is a new low price. The Pro builds on its predecessor with a faster chip and support for Wi-Fi 7. In our testing, it handled multitasking, photo editing, and occasional video editing with ease while still delivering exceptional battery life. It lacks the newer MacBook Pro’s gorgeous OLED display, but its Mini LED screen still looks great, especially given its smooth 120Hz refresh rate. It also offers excellent speakers and a good selection of ports, including three Thunderbolt 4 ports, HDMI, and an SD card slot. Read our review. Apple Watch deals [Product: Apple Watch Series 12 | * The Apple Watch SE 3 is on sale in the 40mm / GPS configuration starting at $179 ($50 off) at Amazon and Walmart, matching its best price to date, while Best Buy is currently $20 higher. Apple’s newest entry-level smartwatch remains our top recommendation for anyone who wants a basic fitness tracker, as it offers all the essentials alongside an always-on display and Apple’s S10 chip, which enables on-device Siri requests. Read our review. AirTags, chargers, and other deals [Product: Apple AirTag (second-gen) | [Product: Baseus AM52 power bank (with built-in cable) | [Product: Apple iPad (11th-gen) | * You can buy the last-gen iPad Mini with 128GB of storage and Wi-Fi on Amazon in select colors for $484 ($115 off), which is the best price we’ve seen since Apple’s recent price hikes. It has a smaller screen and a slower chip than the newer model, and it lacks an OLED screen, the Acoustic Display, and water resistance. Still, it’s a great option for reading and everyday use that’s currently more affordable than its $599 successor, with support for Apple Intelligence and the Apple Pencil Pro. Read our review. * Apple’s latest Magic Mouse is matching its all-time low of $59.99 ($20 off) at Amazon. The wireless mouse features a touch-sensitive surface that lets you scroll through documents and swipe between apps with simple gestures; it also pairs automatically with compatible Macs and offers support for USB-C. articles.title: The tech products we enthusiastically recommend this holiday season | TechCrunch
articles.summary: We've been reviewing a bunch of new gadgets at TechCrunch this year, and we have some clear favorites to share for your Black Friday shopping and beyond.
articles.body:
We’ve been reviewing a bunch of new gadgets and hardware at TechCrunch this year: dumb phones , bird feeders , health trackers , slushy machines , AI mattress pads , you name it. Sometimes we think they’re unnecessary and expensive , but other times, we try out devices that we love so much that we go out and buy them ourselves.

If these products can impress a group of (sometimes) curmudgeonly tech reporters, then they’re sure to please whoever you’re shopping for this holiday season.

We’ve updated this article with new Black Friday pricing for some of our recommendations. Black Friday deals are likely to end by the end of November 30 (Cyber Monday).

We’ve reviewed a lot of e-readers this year. What can we say? We’re nerds. We work for a tech website. But after trying devices from the usual suspects as well as some wildcards, we have recommendations. Evidently, 2026 was the year we fell in love with the pocket-sized e-reader.

Xteink X3 ($55) — a budget pick for someone techy

It’s an e-reader so small that it can fit in your wallet, or even magnetize to the back of your phone. Do you dream of a world where instead of scrolling Instagram when you’re waiting in line for coffee, you actually opt to read books? There’s really something special about the Xteink X3 , and it’s only $55 during Xteink’s Black Friday sale . Fair warning, it takes some fiddling with to set up, and it has no integration with Kindle, Libby, or any other apps, so only buy this for someone willing to do a bit of Reddit browsing and tinkering to get it up and running.

Xteink X4 Pro ($84) — it has a backlight!

If you aren’t planning to magnetize the Xteink to your phone, you’ve got to go with the X4 Pro , which is also discounted for Black Friday . It’s slightly bigger, but it has a backlight, which makes it way more versatile. After using both the X3 and the X4 Pro , I find that the backlight really is a game changer, since I do a lot of reading in bed — plus, I like my Pop Socket wallet a bit too much to displace it for the X3, and I’d rather just carry an extra credit card-sized device than risk forgetting my actual credit and ID cards, which I have grown too used to having on my phone.

Boox Palma Pro 2 ($400) — a phone-sized e-reader without the drawbacks

If I’m being honest, reading my colleague Aisha Malik’s review of the Boox Palma Pro 2 is making me want to buy one. I love using the Xteink e-readers, but they don’t connect to any outside apps. As a hardcore Libby power user (a phrase I am saying in earnest sincerity), it’s a bit frustrating that I can’t get my library books on Xteink e-readers. The same goes for apps like Kobo and Kindle, where any e-book you already own cannot be transferred out of the Amazon ecosystem unless the publisher agrees, which most do not.

If you’re looking for an e-reader with a screen that’s actually book-sized, my favorite that I’ve used is the Kobo Libra Colour , which is $259. The Amazon Paperwhite line is great, but c’mon, Amazon. Branch out!

Hey, we’ve all got to eat. And if you want, you can make that eating process overly techy. Why not?

Ember Mug 3 ($99) — for the tea lover who’s really particular

The Ember Mug 3 is the latest iteration in Ember’s line of coffee/tea cups that actually stay warm. Our reviewer Lauren Forristal especially appreciated that you no longer need to use your phone app to change the mug’s temperature, which seems like it would be really annoying!

This mug is perfect for gifting to someone, or to put on your own wish list — you might not want to spend $99 (or $94 right now for Black Friday ) on a mug for yourself, but these sorts of luxury, nice-to-haves are what holidays are made for!

Ninja Crispi Microwave and Air Fryer ($449.99) — two appliances in one!

Ah, Ninja, the premiere company in the business of turning every appliance into a two-in-one air fryer. I jest, but at least Ninja knows it’s on to something. Despite the Ninja Crispi Microwave and Air Fryer ‘s high price point, Lauren says that this new product made “a pretty convincing case for ditching two appliances and making room for one.” You can’t buy more counter space (without moving), but you can buy more versatile appliances. There’s a $100 off Black Friday deal here .

GoveeLife Smart Nugget Ice Maker Pro ($499.99) — if your fridge has a built-in ice maker, you just won’t understand

Sure, there are cheaper ice makers on the market. But Aisha clarifies that this is the ice maker for “those who crave what’s called ‘the good ice.’” If you feel so passionately about the ice in your beverages that you know what she means, then maybe this is for you. Right now it’s reduced to $349.99 in Amazon’s Black Friday sale .

What they really want is a Mac mini or Claude subscription, but if that’s out of budget, we have some other ideas that might impress your AI-pilled, vibe-coder loved ones …

Open AI Codex Micro ($230) — for the Codex evangelist

When I asked my colleague Lucas Ropek what about his favorite product he reviewed this year, he mentioned the Codex Micro . Some hard-core coders — who the product is aimed toward — have found this thing less than pleasing, but Lucas seems to have had fun figuring out this first attempt by OpenAI at hardware.

Best case, it’s a productivity game-changer for your friend who has a hardworking team of AI agents within the OpenAI ecosystem. Worst case, this will be a great piece of tech history in a few years.

For the person who’s desperate to log off

As people have become more conscious about how much time they spend online, new tech has emerged that, ironically, is designed to keep you away from tech. Some of these products can really make a difference in your life.

Brick ($59) or Brick Night ($129) — a not-so-subtle gift for your friend who doomscrolls every night before bed

For about six months, I’ve consistently used the Brick to prevent me from using social media as the last thing I do before bed, or the first thing in the morning. Some people use it to help them focus during the workday, but evidently, I was not the only one who needed Brick’s help with sleep. The company recently launched its second device, Brick Night , which “Bricks” your phone when you are in the same room. You can customize the times that the Brick Night is active, so it’s not as though you can never, ever use social media in your room. Both Brick and Brick Night are very customizable, so you can create the perfect setup tailored to your needs.

It’s embarrassing how wholeheartedly I recommend the Brick, which is basically just a hunk of plastic with an NFC chip in it and a companion app. But my sleep has improved significantly — I even do 8 a.m. Pilates now. Who am I?

Brick has a small discount to $56.80 for Black Friday on Amazon .

Dumb Phone ($20 + service plan) — for someone who wants to try something new but can’t totally give up their iPhone

I’ve tried out far pricier smart phone alternatives, but the Dumb Phone was both the most affordable, and the most usable for me. In the humble shell of a $20 TCL flip phone , Dumb Co loads its own software so that users can access apps like WhatsApp, Spotify, Apple Music, and Uber. You can even access iMessage through a third-party app, though Apple could probably get that shut down … no one tell Apple, please!

The Dumb Phone is particularly usable because it’s not intended to be a complete replacement for your smartphone — it’s more like a companion device that you can take out with you when you want to feel more present in the world but still may need to call an Uber home.

Wearable health trackers are pretty common nowadays, but after reviewing several different rings and wristbands , Aisha has named a winner.

There are a lot of ugly health trackers. And then there’s the Oura Ring 5 , the leading smart ring maker’s first product that’s thin enough to wear without loudly broadcasting to the world that you’re monitoring your heart rate. (For what it’s worth, I tried the RingConn 3 — which is about the same size as Oura Ring 5 — but returned it, unsatisfied. Womp womp.) Aisha notes in her review that the newest Oura Ring 5 is more durable, has a better battery life, and looks more premium than its predecessors. It’s also part of Amazon’s Black Friday sale, now priced starting at $299 .

This post originally published November 15 and has since been updated to reflect new promotional pricing.

articles.title: Anker’s 100W universal travel charger is down to $60, its lowest price yet
articles.summary: This discounted travel charger from Anker will keep all of your devices topped up on your next vacation with USB-A and USB-C ports to deliver up to 100W.
articles.body: During Black Friday, the Anker 100W Universal Charger is on sale for $59.99 at Amazon, Best Buy, and Walmart, a $20 discount from its list price. That’s a few dollars lower than the previous best, with both the dark gray and silver versions available from all three retailers. With four USB ports and support for over 200 countries, you can keep all of your devices charged wherever you end up. [Product: Anker Universal Charger (100W) | Anker’s travel charger supports outlets in over 200 countries, including Type A for the United States, Canada, Japan, and China; Type C for the European Union; and Type G for the UK and Singapore. It doesn’t support Type I, the outlet used in Australia, New Zealand, and Argentina. Also, there’s no AC adapter. It’s a USB-only affair. To that end, you can charge up to four devices at once, with three USB-C ports and one USB-A port, with two of the USB-C ports capable of delivering up to 100W when used individually. There’s even a tiny display on the unit that lets you check how much power is going to your devices at a glance.

articles.title: Irina Rudakova joins ‘Shayad Yahi Hai Pyaar’ as Zoe; Will her arrival change Preeti and Aarav’s equation?
articles.summary: 'Shayad Yahi Hai Pyaar' has been exploring the many shades of falling in love.
articles.body: 'Shayad Yahi Hai Pyaar' has been exploring the many shades of falling in love. The show has been striking a chord with audiences for its refreshing and emotionally nuanced take on a relationship. Starring Aditi Dev Sharma as Preeti and Daksh Puri as Aarav, the show, an Indian adaptation of the popular Korean drama ‘Something in the Rain’, has made many wonder if love can transcend age. And just when Preeti and Aarav seem to be finding their footing together, their love story is about to encounter another universal relationship hurdle – jealousy.Adding a fresh twist to the narrative is international model and actor Irina Rudakova, who makes her fiction comeback as Zoe, Aarav's former girlfriend from the USA. Confident, glamorous and clear about what she wants, Zoe returns with feelings that are far from resolved. She confides in Preeti that she wants to rekindle her relationship with Aarav and is even considering proposing to him to see if they can give their romance another chance. Her candid revelation leaves Preeti rattled. She begins doubting her place in his life as she is faced with someone who is younger, attractive and shares a romantic history with Aarav.Talking about her return to fiction and joining ‘Shayad Yahi Hai Pyaar’, Irina Rudakova shares, "India has given me so much love over the years, and now getting to tell a love story here feels like everything has come full circle. I am genuinely happy to be back in the fiction arena after exploring different reality formats for quite some time. Having travelled across different parts of the world, I've seen the universal appeal of love as an emotion, but the way it is experienced, expressed and understood in India is very distinct culturally coded. That is something I find particularly beautiful about India. There is an intensity, warmth and emotional depth to relationships here that makes even the simplest moments feel meaningful. And so I am delighted to be strengthening my bond with Indian audiences through this show and hope they enjoy discovering Zoe as much as I have enjoyed bringing her to life."Get the latest TV News, TV Shows and more.
